videos.title: Newport Pier — First benches
videos.scriptPreview: Halfway to the first benches, the water deepens slightly. Surfperch stay in the suds while Pacific sardine schools sometimes push through — great fun on sabiki or small hooks when they are thick.

videos.title: Newport Pier — Mid pier
videos.scriptPreview: Mid pier is prime pelagic territory. Pacific mackerel and sardine run close to the structure in summer and fall. When bonito blitz through, cast a shiny lure fast — they will not wait.

videos.title: Newport Pier — Shore end
videos.scriptPreview: Welcome to Newport Beach Pier. At the shore end, surf anglers target barred surfperch and California corbina in the wash. Light tackle, sand crabs, and fresh mussels are the go-to baits here.

videos.title: Newport Pier — Deep water rail
videos.scriptPreview: Over deeper sand here, California halibut and slot-sized white seabass patrol the bottom. Drop a live sardine or a soft plastic on a Carolina rig and work the edges of the pilings.
